chains.earliest_control: the NAS admin page closed to the internet and reachable from the warehouse network only
chains.name: Warehouse NAS through the forwarded port

steps.text: A routine internet scan of the warehouse's public address finds the NAS's web admin login page answering on the forwarded port.
The attacker tries the maker's known flaws and common passwords against it. One admin password is shared by three shift leads, and the firmware's age is UNKNOWN, so neither defence can be counted on.
None is needed: the shared account is the NAS's administrator, with every share, the camera recordings and the backup settings.

The shares are encrypted for ransom, the client-intake spreadsheet among them. The nightly sync mirrors the encrypted files to the cloud-backup service, and how many earlier versions it keeps is UNKNOWN.

chains.earliest_control: per-person publishing access: the shared SFTP password retired and the agency's CMS admin accounts removed
chains.name: Donate button redirected through the website's shared publishing login

steps.text: The page source names the CMS and its donation plugin, and the host's SFTP service answers on the site's address.
The shared SFTP password, unchanged since the design agency handed over in 2023, or one of the agency's two leftover CMS admin accounts is used. Whether any CMS admin has two-step sign-in is UNKNOWN.
CMS admin access includes the processor plugin's settings page, where its secret API key is stored.
During the holiday drive the donate button is pointed at a look-alike checkout page that keeps card numbers, and the stolen key reads past donation records at the processor.

chains.earliest_control: sign-in blocked on the shared mailboxes, with volunteers reading donations@ through delegated access from accounts of their own
chains.name: Donor mail taken over through the shared donations mailbox

steps.text: The scheduling app's roster gives any volunteer account the names and mobile numbers of the people who triage donor email, and donations@ is printed on every appeal letter.

The donations@ password, shared by three volunteers on personal phones and not changed when volunteers leave, is phished by text or guessed; failed attempts from abroad are already in its sign-in list. Whether it has a second factor registered is UNKNOWN.
A forwarding rule copies incoming donor mail to an outside address. The alert it raises is filed into a folder that is rarely opened.
Mail from donations@, inside the food bank's own threads, asks recurring donors to re-enter their card details on a fake page.
